definition_status: REDEFINED — m7 is now a reproducible MOSES IntDiv1 with a value on disk
definition: IntDiv1 = 1 - mean_{m1,m2 in G} T(m1,m2), MOSES (arXiv:1811.12823); Morgan radius 2 / 1024-bit ECFP4; ordered pairs INCLUDING self-pairs; deterministic subsample (max 300). Implementation: molmetal/scripts/cfm_property_panel.py::internal_diversity, reached via build_panel['aggregate']['internal_diversity'].
why_this_definition: This file previously used 'unit': 'CLI flag count wired-in (count 0-6)'. That is not what the metric's name denotes: m7 DIVERSITY must measure diversity, and a count of wired-in argparse flags measures the trainer's plumbing, not any generated molecule. The number in BLK-C6's title (0.9159 / 0.9215 / 0.8674) came from a throwaway script using 2048-bit Morgan and EXCLUDING self-pairs, i.e. not the reference configuration; it was being read as a strength against a 0.81 target while measuring nothing reproducible.

supersedes.old_protocol: Morgan r=2 / 2048 bit, self-pairs EXCLUDED, ad-hoc script — NOT the MOSES configuration
supersedes.why_retired: unreproducible (the generating script was not kept, and the run cohorts that produced these numbers have no generated_smiles.csv on disk) AND on a non-reference protocol
supersedes.code_moved_to: metrics/by_metric/cfm_internal_diversity_intdiv1.json (side file, Wf 2026-10-10) — that redefinition was real but landed OUTSIDE this canonical slot, so this file kept contradicting it. Merged here.

measured_rows.note: older G4-era run, retained for spread only

FINITE_SAMPLE_WARNING.finding: IntDiv1 is strongly n-dependent, so these cohorts CANNOT be compared to the MOSES 0.857 reference, which is computed over ~1.9M molecules.

measured_on_training_corpus.corpus: molmetal/data/tmqm_dblock_subset.csv (5000 molecules, the project's own d-block training distribution)
measured_on_training_corpus.reading: the SAME corpus rises ~0.044 from n=20 to n=3000 purely from sample size

n_matched_comparison.reading: at every matched n, the generated cohort sits ~0.017 BELOW the training distribution. The delta is stable in n, so it is a property of the cohort, not of the sample size.

FINITE_SAMPLE_WARNING.consequence: The 0.88 'distribution shift' warning threshold from Vendi Score (arXiv:2210.02410) does not apply to an n=37-47 cohort — an n=37 sample of the TRAINING DATA ITSELF already sits at 0.885 and would trip that threshold. No m7 comparison against MOSES/Guan 2023 numbers is valid until a >=1000-molecule generated cohort exists.

correction_to_prior_claim.claim_retracted: cfm_internal_diversity_intdiv1.json's INTERNAL_EVIDENCE asserts 'within our own five runs, IntDiv1 is INVERSELY related to chemical quality' (the best-validity, best-SA run cfm_blk_c5_repair scored lowest, 0.8516).
correction_to_prior_claim.why_retracted: NONE of those five runs has a generated_smiles.csv on disk (molmetal/reports/cfm_fm_ab_2026_10_09/, cfm_fm_control_2026_10_09/, cfm_blk_c5_repair_2026_10_09/, cfm_frag_control/, cfm_frag_assemble/ contain only per_epoch_metrics.{csv,json} + logs). The numbers are not reproducible from disk.
correction_to_prior_claim.on_the_four_cohorts_that_DO_exist: the relationship REVERSES. cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 has both the highest IntDiv1 of the four (0.8690) and among the best SA (4.974) and single-fragment QED (0.2397), while the older wf124_p2_cfm_full has the lowest IntDiv1 (0.8335) and the worst SA (6.489) and worst QED (0.1071). IntDiv1 is POSITIVELY related to quality on the reproducible data.
correction_to_prior_claim.what_survives: the narrow, defensible part — IntDiv is a mode-collapse ALARM, not a quality score, and a high value is not by itself a strength — stands on the MOSES/Vendi literature and needs no project-internal table.

target.note: NO target is asserted. The previously recorded 0.65 (registry) / 0.81 (BLK-C6, Krasnov 2026) / 0.860 (Guan 2023) targets all presume a cohort size comparable to the reference. With n=37-47 they are not measurable, so no target is claimed rather than a target that would be decided in advance.

verdict: MEASURED_NOT_A_CLAIM — m7 now measures its name (IntDiv1 on a real generated cohort) and the number is neither a strength nor a weakness. It is a collapse alarm, and at the cohort sizes that currently exist it cannot be compared to any published value.

diversity_term_wiring.note: The 6 trainer diversity flags (top-p / top-k / temperature / mmd-weight / repulsion-weight / scaffold-conditioning) remain wired in molmetal/scripts/train_cfm_yuelbond_wasserstein.py per Wf-388-A2, all default OFF, diversity_term == 0 when all OFF. That wiring is preserved and is a TRAINER-side fact. It is simply no longer what this metric file reports — the previous conflation of 'flag count' with 'm7 value' is what made the metric unreadable.

restore_condition: m7 becomes comparable to published values when a generated_smiles.csv with >=1000 unique molecules exists (a GPU run with --gen-validity-samples >= 1000 --save-generated-smiles). At that n the finite-sample curve has flattened (0.9079 at n=1000 vs 0.9101 at n=3000) and an n-matched training-distribution control can be run in the same call, making the MOSES comparison valid. CPU-only today; BLOCKED on GPU (AGENTS.md 5.1).
tests: molmetal/tests/test_m7_internal_diversity.py (7, MEASURED 7 passed in 0.68s on 2026-10-11) — includes the MOSES-configuration check (1024 bits, radius 2, self-pairs on), total-collapse -> 0.0 rather than None, and the 1-1/n ceiling.
not_comparable_with: metrics/by_metric/diversity_tanimoto.json (0.1366) — that is the Lambda MCTS GA/search path, a different protocol; the low value there is the diagnostic one per the same literature.

cross_references.csv_reader: cfm_property_panel.read_smiles_csv (last_epoch=True selects the final checkpoint; these CSVs are single-epoch so pooled == last)
